children: Oil prices fell Monday as traders weighed prospects for increased Russian diesel supplies and a potential Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire against persistent Middle East supply risks.
December Brent crude futures fell 0.2% to $104.53 a barrel, while December West Texas Intermediate futures dropped 0.4% to $90.69 a barrel.

Brent briefly climbed above $105.50 a barrel overnight following attacks on Riyadh's international airport before reversing gains, according to Saxo Bank. Russia's partial lifting of its diesel-export ban also provided modest downward pressure on oil prices, the bank said.

President Trump said Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to stop attacking each other's energy facilities, although Moscow hasn't confirmed an agreement. The announcement followed a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday under which Russia would supply more than 300,000 metric tons of diesel to U.S. and global markets, followed by another 500,000 tons in November.

The prospective Russian diesel exports could provide some relief to a market facing fuel shortages, though their impact will depend on Ukraine's continued attacks on Russian oil infrastructure, Vivek Dhar, a commodity analyst at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, said in a research note.

Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation said an attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday killed 12 people and injured 309 others. The airport was targeted again Sunday, when another attack killed one person and injured 11, the authority said.

Attacks on oil tankers also continued over the weekend. The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said a tanker near Oman's Sohar anchorage was struck by an uncrewed aerial vehicle Sunday. Another tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile while transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz, causing  damage to the vessel. The crew of the second tanker was reported safe, the agency said.
